page.layout: One page of text in one column. Running head at top, with the page number at top right. Below the last line: the signature "K 4" at the centre left and the catchword "rectas" at the right. No margin notes.

main_text.p: bus quam tutissime navigari solet; ac inde Lutetiam usque, pedestri itinere, facillime ut opinor, atque expeditissime ad te perveniet, quod jam expectas feliciter, ni fallor, allaturus, illud namque in clusum capsula, & adversus pluvias, aliosque hujusmodi sinistros casus optime munitum, illi tradidi; non laborabo de Pentateuchi locis, quæcumque enim extant in hoc textu, animadversione digna, tibimet proprlis oculis intueri licebit; tantum dicā, ea omnia errata, quæ in ἀπογραφῷ [?] jam missō adnotasti, in hoc exemplari meo ita prorsus se habere, me reperisse, sicut tu corrigenda esse prudenter existimaveras. De pronunciatione vocalium apud Samaritanos nihil ausim [?] dicere, cum neque eorum Linguam intelligam, neque illos legentes unquam audiverim; illud tantum observavi, hujusce exemplaris mei scriptorem, in quibusdam dictionibus, quas evolvendo libro facile reperies, super aliquas literas virgulas quasdam, seu lineolas apposuisse, vel jacentes, vel dextrorsum aliquantulum e-[?]

page.notes: The scan is slightly blurred at the right, with a grey stain and show-through at the right edge; these are not text. "ἀπογραφῷ" is in italic and partly blurred, so the final letters are uncertain. "ausim" is read from a blurred word. The last word on the page is hyphenated at the line end, and the catchword "rectas" confirms the continuation "e-". The reading of the final hyphenated letter is uncertain. The word "missō" may be "missō" with a macron, which is also uncertain. The word after "in hoc" is set in italic-like type and is clear enough. The Greek word has an acute accent on its last letter that is hard to see.
